overview: Explanatory sequential mixed methods evaluation of weekly electronic symptom reporting in the breast and colorectal clinics: a quantitative strand on completion and alert response for all patients treated from March 2026 to February 2027, followed by a qualitative strand of interviews with patients who stopped reporting and with triage nurses, integrated in a joint display.
population: Quantitative: every adult who started chemotherapy in the two clinics between 1 March 2026 and 28 February 2027 and was offered weekly reporting (about 420 patients). Qualitative: 20 to 24 patients who stopped reporting before finishing treatment, sampled by age, deprivation and preferred language, and 10 to 12 triage nurses.
exposure: Weekly reporting as delivered; for the mechanism analysis, an unanswered severe alert (no nurse contact recorded within 24 hours) in the previous week.
procedures: Monthly platform exports under DA-2026-17 give expected and completed reports and alert timestamps; the triage log gives nurse contact times. Interviews run from March to May 2027 by telephone or in clinic, with interpreters where needed, using a topic guide informed by the quantitative results. Integration uses a joint display that sets each quantitative pattern beside the interview themes that explain or contradict it.

outcomes.name: Report completion over the first 12 weeks
outcomes.measure: Completed divided by expected weekly reports per patient
outcomes.why: Completion is the precondition for any benefit and the quantity falling in routine care (claim c2).

outcomes.name: Time from severe alert to nurse contact
outcomes.measure: Hours from alert timestamp to first recorded contact, weekday and weekend separately
outcomes.why: The step where the loop breaks (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Emergency visits or unplanned admissions
outcomes.measure: Any emergency department visit or unplanned admission during the first 12 weeks, described by completion group
outcomes.why: The outcome patients and the centre care about, described without a causal claim.

outcomes.name: Reasons for stopping and ways alerts are handled
outcomes.measure: Themes from interviews with patients and triage nurses

outcomes.name: Triage nurse time spent on alerts
outcomes.measure: Minutes per week logged on alert handling
outcomes.why: Changes to the response standard must not overwhelm nurses.

feasibility: Exports already exist; one protected day a week covers the analysis and 30 to 36 interviews over three months.
biasMitigation: Completion defined before exports are examined
Mechanism analysis adjusts for the severity of the previous report
Purposive sampling that includes older, more deprived and interpreter-dependent patients
A second coder for a quarter of transcripts

biasFlags.label: Confounding by illness severity
biasFlags.note: Sicker patients both trigger unanswered alerts and stop reporting; severity of the last report is adjusted for.

biasFlags.label: Interviewer is a clinical colleague
biasFlags.note: Nurses may soften criticism; interviews with nurses are done by a researcher outside the unit.

flags: One primary outcome for the quantitative strand; the qualitative strand is reported as themes
parsimony.simplestPath: Two clinics, one completion measure, one mechanism analysis, one round of interviews.

theoreticalFramework: COM-B to organise reasons for stopping (capability, opportunity, motivation) in the interview guide and the joint display; no other framework.
summary: Sequential mixed methods: completion and alert response for about 420 patients, then 30 to 36 interviews, integrated in a joint display.
